merge_corrections.what: NO CORRECTION NEEDED. Zero errors and zero warnings on the gate, including the two checks added in the previous 24 hours that this platform's other files failed: control text is unique on all twenty processes, and no judgment citation is shared by more than one. This is the second submission in the campaign to need nothing changed at merge, and the first from this platform.
accepted_from_submitter: 15.3.2 keeps the commodity asymmetry straight in both directions: gas distribution integrity reporting is a federal duty under 49 CFR 192.1007(e) and (g) and 191.11, and IEEE 1366 is named as a method that is NOT a federal filing mandate. Getting the negative right is harder than getting the citation right.

15.3.3 separates 18 CFR 125.3's continuing-plant-inventory retention from the shorter periods for work and authorisation records, and confines 49 CFR 192.709(a) service-life retention to transmission pipe rather than spreading it over the distribution record set.

Six SPEC processes, each justified either as a standing capability with no instance boundary or as a measure family whose formulas are member-gated and were not reproduced. 15.2.1 to 15.2.3 name EN 15341 and SMRP metrics by number and refuse to print the arithmetic, which is exactly what the ceiling requires.
15.5.5 draws the distinction that makes an interface model worth having: a transport acknowledgement is not evidence that the receiving record passed semantic and authority checks.
merge_corrections.models_built_here: Seven artifacts, 5 BPMN and 2 CMMN. The specification names them; only this side has the generator.

derivation: STANDARDS-DERIVED. Every field traces to a standard, a regulation, a recognised industry body or an explicit judgment. No client programme or product practice enters this specification.
taxonomy_origin: TAXONOMY ORIGIN, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT FACT FROM THE DERIVATION ABOVE. The derivation line describes where FIELD CONTENT comes from: every field value traces to a standard, a regulation or a recognised industry body and carries its citation. It does NOT describe where the taxonomy comes from. Which processes exist, how they are grouped and what they are called is a practitioner synthesis of delivered implementations, generalised until it is product- and client-neutral. Of the 102 process groups, 43 originate in programme material, 28 in domain research, 20 in a published source and 11 in folder and file names; the provenance layer grades every one and names what to read next. This model is DELIVERED PRACTICE SPECIFIED AGAINST STANDARDS, not a standard turned into a model - and saying so is not a weakness. A taxonomy proven in delivery and then held against the standards is a stronger claim than one derived from a standard and never built.
field_set: EN 17007:2017 cl. 5.2 maintenance process profile, corroborated by ISO 9001:2015 cl. 4.4.1 a) to h).
gaps: No permitted source defines one operational-reporting semantic model, issue calendar, ad-hoc analysis method or self-service governance model for gas and electric distribution. Report routes, populations and publication controls are judgment.

EN 15341 indicator names and SMRP metric numbers are available, but the relevant formulas are paywalled or member-gated. This specification names them without reproducing calculation logic; each operator must control its executable definitions.
No permitted source defines first-time-fix or a cross-commodity rule for linking repeat intervention to rework. Process 15.2.3 therefore remains SPEC rather than inventing a decision model.

Federal reporting is asymmetric. 49 CFR 192.1007(e) and (g) and 191.11 prescribe gas distribution integrity reporting; IEEE 1366 supplies an electric reliability method but not a federal filing duty for local distribution.

No permitted source supplies a complete retention schedule for every report, work record, attachment and audit record. 18 CFR 125.3 and 49 CFR 192.709 cover named records with different scopes and periods; the remaining schedule is unresolved here.

GFMAM subjects 5.1 to 5.4 establish data strategy, standards, management and systems as capabilities but do not prescribe master-data ownership, stewardship, quality thresholds, reference-code life cycle, organisational scope or access-review methods.

IEC 61968-6 standardises electric work interfaces only. There is no gas work or work-task information model, and no cross-commodity contract for asset, spatial, time, cost, document, procurement, invoice or ledger content.

IEC 61968-6 cl. 4.2 has no component for document management, procurement or an integration service. Documentation and interface coordination are placed on MAI and supply transactions on MM without inventing component codes.

No permitted source prescribes interface-health measures, delivery guarantees, retry, duplicate handling, idempotency, semantic reconciliation or exception-aging rules. Process 15.5.5 is judgment beyond the named exchange structures.
GFMAM subject 2.3 Asset Management Assurance and Audit remains partial: this category retains reporting evidence but has no process that assures the asset management system as a whole.

GFMAM subject 7.1 Outcomes and Impacts remains partial: operational measures are reported, but the taxonomy has no distinct process for tracing asset-management outcomes and impacts to stakeholder value.

APQC PCF Utilities v7.2.1 14.1.3 Perform operations performance management (pcf_id 11268) includes activity 19273 Plan and manage control room operations, which has no group here. It may belong at the Category 18 network-operations boundary rather than in performance reporting.

The boundary between 15.1 operational reporting and 15.3 obligation reporting is audience-based, while EN 17007 DTA.11 treats calculation, storage and access as one process. Shared calculations must not fork across the two groups.

Processes 15.5.4 and 15.5.6 combine domain ownership with interface transport. EN 17007 places documentation in DOC and spare-parts purchasing in SPP, while this taxonomy places both exchanges under integration; ownership must remain with the source domain.

processes.name: Exchange work and activity information
processes.intent: Exchange work requests, orders, tasks and activity records between authorised operational components.
activities: Receive or detect a work-information exchange event
Validate the source, verb and required identifiers
Transform only through an approved mapping
Deliver the payload and record its exchange status
Confirm acceptance or route an exception for reconciliation

trigger.text: A component creates, changes, cancels, closes or requests work information.

inputs.what: Source work payload and exchange verb

controls.text: Preserve the work identity, source component, verb and exchange result so duplicate or rejected messages differ from accepted changes.
IEC 61968-6 standardises exchange structures and verbs, not the internal work process or a gas work-item model.

measures.name: Information and communication technology indicators
measures.definition: Use the applicable EN 15341 ICTi indicator; formulas are not reproduced.

measures.name: Work Order Cycle Time
measures.definition: Use SMRP 5.4.7 for completed work; formula not reproduced.

variants: Create a new work request in the receiving component
Change an existing work or task record
Cancel work before execution
Close work and publish the final activity record

notation.why: A message follows validation, mapping, delivery and acknowledgement with a defined exception route.

processes.name: Exchange asset and spatial information
processes.intent: Exchange asset identity, attributes, location and spatial relationships while preserving source authority.
activities: Receive the asset or spatial change event
Validate identity, source authority and location reference
Map approved asset and spatial fields
Deliver the change to the consuming register
Reconcile acceptance, rejection or conflicting authority

trigger.text: An authorised asset or spatial record is created, changed or retired.

controls.text: Preserve the authoritative identity and source for each attribute; a consuming register does not overwrite a governed source without an approved correction.
Keep asset identity and spatial position linked to the work or field evidence that changed them.

measures.name: Information and communication technology indicators
measures.definition: Use the applicable EN 15341 ICTi indicator; formulas are not reproduced.

measures.name: Rework
measures.definition: Use SMRP 4.1 for repeated corrective work; formula not reproduced.

variants: New asset and location published after acceptance
Attribute change propagated without a location change
Spatial change propagated without asset replacement
Retired asset removed from active views but retained in history

notation.why: An authorised asset change follows validation, mapping, delivery and reconciliation on a known path.

processes.name: Exchange time, cost and financial information
processes.intent: Exchange approved labour time, material cost and financial coding against the correct work and plant records.
activities: Receive approved time or cost information
Validate work, person, material and financial identifiers
Apply the approved accounting and interface mapping
Deliver the transaction to the receiving component
Record acceptance or route a reconciliation exception

trigger.text: Approved time, material or cost information is ready for financial exchange.

controls.text: Preserve the work identity, approved source, account mapping and acceptance result for each exchanged time or cost transaction.
For regulated plant accounting, retain the work and plant linkage required by 18 CFR 101 and supporting records under 18 CFR 125.3.

measures.name: Information and communication technology indicators
measures.definition: Use the applicable EN 15341 ICTi indicator; formulas are not reproduced.

measures.name: Work Order Cycle Time
measures.definition: Use SMRP 5.4.7 for completed work; formula not reproduced.

variants: Approved labour time posted to work
Material issue or return posted with cost
Contract or service cost applied to completed work
Financial coding exception returned for correction

notation.why: Approved transactions follow validation, mapping, delivery and reconciliation on a repeatable path.

processes.name: Exchange document and attachment content
processes.intent: Exchange controlled document references and attachments with their work, revision and access context intact.
activities: Receive the document or attachment exchange request
Validate work linkage, revision, content type and access
Transmit the content or controlled reference
Record receipt, rejection and version context
Reconcile missing, superseded or unauthorised content

trigger.text: A work process publishes or requests a controlled document or attachment.

outputs.what: Accepted document or attachment with linkage

controls.text: Preserve the work link, revision, source, content type and access decision with every exchanged document or attachment.
IEC 61968-6 has no document-management component or document-content payload; MAI carries the operational linkage without implying a content model.

measures.name: Information and communication technology indicators
measures.definition: Use the applicable EN 15341 ICTi indicator; formulas are not reproduced.

measures.name: Rework
measures.definition: Use SMRP 4.1 for repeated corrective work; formula not reproduced.

variants: Controlled document reference exchanged without copying content
Attachment content exchanged and linked to a work activity
Superseded revision rejected and current revision requested
Access-restricted content withheld with an exception record

notation.why: A content request follows validation, transmission, receipt and reconciliation on a known path.

processes.name: Monitor interface health and reconcile exceptions
processes.intent: Detect failed or inconsistent exchanges, determine their disposition, and restore agreement between affected records.
activities: Detect an unavailable, rejected, duplicate or inconsistent exchange
Establish affected records and the last accepted state
Investigate transport, mapping, authority and data causes
Correct, replay, supersede or reject under approved authority
Verify both sides and close or escalate the exception

trigger.text: An interface monitor or consuming component reports a failed or inconsistent exchange.

inputs.what: Interface event, status and diagnostic evidence
Source and target work or asset records
Approved mapping and last accepted state

outputs.what: Reconciled records and verified exchange state

controls.text: Establish the last accepted state and authoritative source before replaying or correcting an exchange.
Do not treat a transport acknowledgement as evidence that the receiving record passed semantic and authority checks.

measures.name: Information and communication technology indicators
measures.definition: Use the applicable EN 15341 ICTi indicator; formulas are not reproduced.

measures.name: Rework
measures.definition: Use SMRP 4.1 for repeated corrective work; formula not reproduced.

variants: Transient delivery failure corrected by controlled replay
Duplicate exchange retained once without a second state change
Semantic mismatch corrected at the authoritative source
Conflicting authority escalated without automatic overwrite

notation.why: Cause, evidence and correction order vary legitimately across transport, mapping, authority and data exceptions.

processes.name: Exchange procurement, invoice and ledger transactions
processes.intent: Exchange approved supply, invoice and ledger transactions while preserving work, material and financial references.
activities: Receive an approved supply or financial transaction
Validate supplier, material, work and financial references
Map the transaction to the receiving record
Deliver and record the acceptance result
Return rejection or mismatch for correction and reconciliation

trigger.text: An approved purchase, receipt, invoice or ledger transaction is ready for exchange.

outputs.what: Accepted procurement, invoice or ledger transaction

controls.text: Preserve the supplier, material or service, receipt, work, account and acceptance references needed to trace the transaction.
IEC 61968-6 has MM and FIN components but no procurement, invoice or ledger payload; a work payload is not a transaction standard.

measures.name: Information and communication technology indicators
measures.definition: Use the applicable EN 15341 ICTi indicator; formulas are not reproduced.

measures.name: Work Order Cycle Time
measures.definition: Use SMRP 5.4.7 for completed work; formula not reproduced.

variants: Purchase or service commitment sent for financial recording
Receipt or service acceptance matched to originating work
Invoice matched and accepted for posting
Ledger transaction rejected for a missing or conflicting reference

notation.why: An approved transaction follows validation, mapping, delivery, matching and exception return on a repeatable path.
